**Predicting several future positions during training asks the representation to carry information beyond the immediate next token.** Auxiliary heads or sequential prediction modules add losses for farther-ahead targets. Their conditioning differs by architecture, so “multi-token prediction” does not specify one exact model. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.19437)

For a simple illustration, the representation after a prefix may be trained to predict both the next token and the token after it. That can encourage anticipation of longer structure, but the additional objective can also conflict with the main one if poorly weighted.

**At inference, proposals still need verification for exact speculative decoding.** Extra modules may propose a short sequence cheaply. A target-model procedure accepts or corrects it according to the appropriate rule; merely outputting all auxiliary predictions does not preserve the target distribution.

Speed depends on proposal acceptance, extra computation, batch size, and the target's bottleneck. Measure final task quality and end-to-end latency. Predicting four tokens internally does not imply a fourfold serving speedup, especially when verification or rejected proposals consume much of the saved work.

**Technical details and references.**

Multi-token prediction adds training objectives for future positions beyond the next token, encouraging the representation to capture information useful over a longer horizon. Architectures differ: independent auxiliary heads and sequential prediction modules condition on different information, so their exact loss and inference behavior must be specified. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.19437)

The extra modules can propose several tokens for speculative decoding. A target-model verification procedure is still needed to preserve the target distribution; auxiliary predictions are not automatically exact samples. Benefits depend on acceptance rate, extra-head compute, batch size, and target bottlenecks. Additional prediction losses can improve learned representations in reported settings but may conflict with the primary objective if poorly weighted. Evaluate both final-model quality and end-to-end decode speed instead of equating more predicted tokens with proportional speedup.
